response.summary: All three digests match. Judged beside the five phase records (004, 008, 011, 015, 020), the shipped paths they name (src/gnd/rmap.py, src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/export/ossie_relational.py, src/gnd/export/physical_binding.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/input_policy.py), the normative sections and the cited tests. Every completion predicate as amended by plan section 11 has evidence that would fail if false: the three legacy files are pinned byte-for-byte with --ontology-only and without --physical-binding (test_t6_ontology_only_equals_the_ob1_baseline, test_t7_without_the_flag_the_relational_files_equal_the_baseline over the 82-entry baselines); read_binding is total over arbitrary bytes, each refusal a named BindingError rule (test_t8_arbitrary_bytes_are_refused_by_name, r1-F1/F2 regressions); is_regular_identifier and _quoted match the OB5 record, the oracle-lane note and the normative text; the A1-A16 amendments are each supported by the record that raised them, with the r2 wording kept above section 11; every Q-id raised in the records is dispositioned; missing external acceptance is stated plainly, not implied to be met. In the files the results list as carrying no review opinion I found no behavioural defect. Four low completeness items on the plan and delta follow; none blocks the demonstration.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

Does every completion predicate in the plan (as amended by section 11) have evidence in the results that would fail if the predicate were false? Read the phase records 004-phase-OB1.md, 008-phase-OB2.md, 011-phase-OB3.md, 015-phase-OB4.md, 020-phase-OB5.md and the tests they cite before judging.

Do the shipped code paths (src/gnd/rmap.py; src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/export/ossie_relational.py, src/gnd/export/physical_binding.py; src/gnd/commands/export.py; src/gnd/ossie_import.py and src/gnd/input_policy.py) behave as the results and delta say? In particular: a run without --physical-binding and with --ontology-only must write the bytes it wrote before the milestone; the binding reader must be total over arbitrary bytes; and every table or column name must be quoted in Ossie's normalized form.

The results list files that carry no review opinion (repairs made after the last phase review read them). Read src/gnd/export/physical_binding.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/input_policy.py and is_regular_identifier and _quoted in src/gnd/export/ossie_relational.py with that in mind, and report any defect.

Do the pages (representation-format.md sections 'Relational mapping (Rmap)' and 'Ossie interchange'; docs/explanation/ossie.md; the two how-to pages; the Ossie section of src/gnd/skills/gnd-export/SKILL.md; the release-note section) state what the code does, each rule in one home?

Is every open question raised in the milestone's records dispositioned in the results (closed, carried with an owner, or an accepted residual), and is any disposition wrong? Is the missing external acceptance stated plainly and not implied to be met?
Are the close amendments in plan section 11 each supported by the record that raised them, with the prior wording kept?
Every concern's evidence must cite one of the three named files; name the record, code or test line in the observation.
